item.title: International Business in a Reconfiguring Southeast Asia
item.content:encoded:
S. Tamer Cavusgil, Georgia State University

Marleen Dieleman, IMD Business School

Md. Tareq Hossain, Thammasat University

Ruey-Jer "Bryan" Jean, National Taiwan University

Destan Kandemir, Georgia State University

Suntichai Kotcharin, Thammasat University

Hussain Rammal, Adelaide University

Southeast Asia is a significant yet understudied region in international business, despite forming the world's fifth-largest economic bloc and attracting record foreign investment. While the region presents unique theoretical challenges through supply chain reconfiguration, rising regional multinationals, and institutional diversity, scholarship on emerging markets remains dominated by China and India with limited Southeast Asian representation in top journals.

This focused issue seeks theory-building contributions that treat Southeast Asian phenomena as intellectually generative rather than merely illustrative. The collection particularly welcomes work by scholars based in the region and aims to develop international business frameworks beyond existing emerging-market vocabulary. Four themes guide submissions: internationalization of Southeast Asian multinationals, supply chain governance and maritime connectivity, geopolitical hedging dynamics, and indigenous theorizing grounded in regional intellectual traditions and methodologies.

Appel publié par Management International Review. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Rise and internationalization of Southeast Asian multinationals
  • Supply chain reconfiguration and regional governance
  • Cross-border trade and geopolitics
  • Indigenous theorizing and methodological innovation
  • ASEAN economies and FDI
  • Digital-native champions and platform expansion
  • State-linked enterprises internationalization
  • Supply chain resilience and maritime logistics
  • Middle-power firm strategies and hedging
  • Non-market strategy under geopolitical pressure
  • Indigenous concepts in IB theory
  • Postcolonial perspectives on knowledge production
